body:
## Problem

`detect_holes` on a Drill operation takes holes that are larger than the drill. `generate` and `verify` then pass with no warning, and `post` writes the program. Each such hole is drilled at the drill diameter, so the finished hole is too small. Nothing tells the user.

This is the Drill twin of #1556 (Bore), which is closed.

## Reproduction (main at 983f527bd, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

Part: a plate 120 x 80 x 10 mm with a boss, exported from SolidCraft as STEP. Through holes: two of D6, two of D8, two of D12.

```
import_model   { "path": "platte_zapfen.step", "name": "Platte" }
fit_stock      { "sides": [2, 2, 2, 2, 0, 0] }
add_tool       { "catalog": "DR-0600" }
add_operation  { "kind": "drill", "tool": "DR-0600", "source": "Platte", "name": "Bohren" }
detect_holes   { "name": "Bohren" }        -> "holes": 6, "skipped": []
generate       { "name": "Bohren" }        -> status ok, warnings []
```

The operation holds holes of radius 3, 4 and 6 (D6, D8, D12). The cache has six `deep` cycles and no warning.

## Expected result

One of these, by name:

- `detect_holes` skips a hole whose diameter is not the drill diameter (within a tolerance), and lists it in `skipped` with the reason (for example "D8.000 hole, D6.000 drill"), or
- `generate` refuses the operation by name, or
- the operation gets a warning that names each undersize hole (for a pilot drill, a user can accept it).

## Proposed priority

`P3` by the AGENTS.md table: a wrong part size with no message, and a workaround (pick the holes by hand). The tool path itself does not gouge or collide.

body:
## Request

Add a post for Mach3 Mill (3-axis). Mach3 is still on many retrofit mills and routers. The `Mach4` post writes words and macros that Mach3 does not read in the same way.

## Differences to the Mach4 post

From the public "Using Mach3Mill" manual (behaviour only):

- Canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98` / `G99`. `G84` needs a tapping head setup: refuse a tap by name unless the machine file says that tapping is available.
- `G4 P` dwell: Mach3 reads P in seconds or in milliseconds by a setting ("G04 dwell param in ms"). The post must have an option for this. Default: seconds, as in the manual.
- Tool change: `T<n> M6`, then `G43 H<n>`. The `M6` behaviour depends on the user's `M6Start` / `M6End` macros, so the post does not assume a retract inside `M6`. It retracts first.
- Arcs: the IJ mode (absolute or incremental) is a Mach3 setting. The post must not depend on it: it writes the IJ mode word that the user selects in an option (default incremental IJ). The goldens must be checked against the manual for the word that Mach3 reads. A header comment names the mode.
- No Custom Macro B (`#` variables in expressions). The Mach4 post uses `[...]` expressions in some places; the Mach3 post must write plain numbers only.
- Program end `M30`. Comments `( )`.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Mach3` and a machine file.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill, peck, bore, two tools, and the dwell option in both modes.
- A test that no `[` expression and no `#` variable is posted.

## Request

Add a post for classic Grbl 1.1 (3-axis mill). Many small routers and hobby mills run Grbl 1.1 on an Arduino-class board. The `grblHAL` post (#710) writes words that Grbl 1.1 refuses, so it is not a replacement.

From the public Grbl 1.1 documentation (the "Commands" and "Interface" wiki pages, behaviour only):

- No `M6`. A tool change is `M5`, a retract to a safe Z in machine coordinates (`G53 G0 Z...`), then `M0` with a comment that names the tool. `T` is written in a comment only.
- No `G43 H`. The length offset is `G43.1 Z...` or nothing. Default: write no length offset (the user zeroes each tool), and write `G49` in the preamble.
- No `O` program number. No `G41` / `G42`. No `G98` / `G99`.
- `G4 P` is in seconds.
- Line buffer of 80 characters: keep each block short. Comments are `( )` only. Do not write comments with nested brackets.
- Coolant: `M7`, `M8`, `M9` only. Other coolant kinds are refused by name.

## Acceptance

- A built-in post `Grbl 1.1` and a machine file `grbl-3axis.mch`.
- Goldens for contour, pocket, drill (expanded), peck (expanded), bore with dwell, two tools.
- A test that each posted line is 80 characters or less, and that no unsupported word (`G8x`, `M6`, `G43 H`, `G41`, `G42`, `O`) is posted.

title: 2D Contour tabs: the bridge on the part is tab width minus the tool diameter; a tab width <= D leaves no tab and frees the part

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Problem

2D Contour tabs are narrower than the "Tab width" that the user sets. At its narrowest section (the centre line of the cut channel) the tab is `tab_width - tool diameter` wide. When the tab width is equal to or less than the tool diameter, no tab stays. The part comes free during the last levels, and no message tells the user.

## Cause

`Ring::tab_keeps` and `Ring::tab_keeps_from_start` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring.rs`) measure the tab window on the tool-centre ring. At each end of that window the cutter disc removes `D/2` more material along the centre line of the channel. The bridge is thus `tab_width` wide at the part wall, but only `tab_width - D` wide at the channel centre line.

Example: a 6 mm end mill and a tab width of 5 mm. The window on the centre path is 5 mm long. On the channel centre line the cutter removes 3 mm on each side past the window ends. The two cuts overlap by 1 mm (5 - 6 = -1 mm), so the bridge is cut through.

## Expected result

The tab width is the smallest width of the bridge that stays. For this, the window on the centre ring must be `tab_width + D` long.

If a tab cannot stay (for example, the window with the tool diameter is longer than the tab spacing), refuse the operation by name. Do not cut the part free silently.

## Related

- #1565: Verify and the stock sim do not find a piece of stock that the program frees. Thus this defect is not found by verify either.

## Proposed priority

`P1` by the AGENTS.md table: wrong output that passes. A freed part can move into the cutter.

I can make the fix and a test (shape-mask test of the bridge width) in a PR from my fork.

body:
## What changed

PR #2035 (merge commit `983f527bd`) changed the Adaptive strategy of the 3D Pocket operation. The tool disc now goes past the stock side. It cuts the stock ring from the air.

- Operation and strategy: 3D Pocket, `PocketStrategy::Adaptive`, whole model only (not shell, not rest roughing). See `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:846`.
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band (`r - OPEN_SLACK`).
- Reach constant: `ADAPTIVE_BAND_PER_R = 2.0` at `crates/motion/src/machining3d/open_side.rs:67`. The band is `2 * r + OPEN_SLACK` (`stock_band`, line 71). `OPEN_SLACK` is 0.01 mm (line 34).
- Default: the reach is always on for this strategy. It is a `pub const`, not an operation parameter. A user cannot change it.
- The planner reads a wider air band of `stock.offset(4.0 * r)` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs:84`.
- The reach applies on each level down to the bottom (review note 4).

## What a user sees today

- A tagged fixture box that meets the band in XY and stands above the operation bottom refuses the operation at generation. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` (`crates/app/src/operation/open_side.rs:98`, function `air_band_refusal`). The machine table is skipped.
- A vise or clamp with no fixture model: no note, no warning and no refusal was found in the diff or on `origin/main`. The check reads only tagged fixture boxes (`air_band_refusal`, line 64).
- No check can see a vise that has no model. The PR body says the post gate is not changed. Whether the post gate or the simulation has another check for this case: not confirmed.
- The only notice is the changelog row of PR #2035. It says the tool goes up to 2 tool radii past the stock side.
- A collision with a modelled fixture is refused at generation. A collision with the part is held by the plan's own law. Both are outside the defect floor. This issue is a design question, not a defect.

## The open question

How does the product handle a vise that has no model when the tool goes 2 tool radii past the stock side? Options:

1. Keep the reach as it is. Rely on the changelog row and on the fixture refusal.
2. Make the reach a user parameter of the operation, with a default. The default can be off or on.
3. Limit the reach when no fixture model exists in the document. For example, use the old band of `r - OPEN_SLACK` then.
4. Show a warning when the reach is used and no fixture model exists.

Options 2 to 4 can combine. The maintainer decides. Related issue: #339 (Handle fixtures/vises). This issue is not a duplicate of #339. #339 asks for fixture modelling. This issue asks what the operation does while no model exists.

Done means: the maintainer picks an option and the work is filed or done.

## Source

- Review comment, note 4: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2035#issuecomment-6972199583

Parametric tools remain and can serve as components.

**Reference:** ISO 13399 (cutting tool data representation: tool items, adaptive items, coordinate systems and connection interfaces). Clean-room: no competitor material.

1. **Auto counts the air above the hole as depth.** The auto law reads depth as R plane - bottom. `generate` with no name is documented as regenerating "every operation that is not current". ## Expected

One `generate` with no name leaves every operation current: it regenerates in program order and includes the operations that went stale because an earlier one changed.

A 2D Contour on a whole model (no picks) takes its ring from the part's section at Top Z and walks it only while the wall it trims stands at the same place (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs`). When the part grows outward below that plane - a chamfer, a step, a slot floor - the ring stops there. Bottom Z, the step-down ladder and the tabs below that level are dropped with no note: generate says ok, verify says ok, and the "outside contour" leaves the part attached and its sides unfinished.

Two cases on the same part:

1. **Default Top Z (top_of_model, z 15):** the section at z 15 is the island's top face, so the contour runs **one loop around the island at Z-2 (z 15) only** - no step-downs, nothing on the plate outline, no tabs, though Bottom Z is -0.5 and tab_count 4. (The island widens below z 15 because of its chamfer, so the ring stops at once.)
2. **Top Z = bottom_of_model + 10 (plate top):** the section at z 10 includes the open slot notch. The ring runs Z-7, Z-9, Z-10 (z 10, 8, 7) and stops at the **slot floor** (z 7), where the plate outline closes. The plate sides from z 7 down to -0.5 are never cut and no tab move is written.

## Expected

The outside profile of the part from Top Z down to Bottom Z (-0.5), with the 4 tabs in the bottom 1.5 mm - each level using the part's outline at that level - or, if a ring cannot go deeper, a finding that names the level it stopped at and why (the Prime Directive: mark it incomplete rather than post a silently partial path).

## Repro (MCP)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

- `add_tool {catalog: "EM-1000-4FL"}`
- Case 1: `add_operation {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-1000-4FL", source: "flange", params: {bottom_z: {reference: "bottom_of_model", offset: -0.5}, stepdown: 3.5, tab_count: 4}}`, `generate`, `verify`, `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`
- Case 2: same with `top_z: {reference: "bottom_of_model", offset: 10}, stepdown: 2, tab_count: 4, tab_width: 6, tab_height: 1.5`

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09)

Case 1 - the whole operation:
```
G0 X83.216 Y11.178 Z0
G1 X83.216 Y11.178 Z-2 F300
G1 X25 Y10.999 Z-2 F1200
G2 X15.999 Y20 Z-2 I0 J9.001
...
G0 X67.225 Y10.655 Z25
```
(X15.999..84.001, Y10.999..49.001 = the island top outline offset by r 5; one level only.)

Case 2 - three levels, deepest Z-10 (world z 7, the slot floor):
```
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-7 F300   ... loop with the notch G2 X90 Y60 / X95 Y65 ...
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-9 F300   ...
G1 X89.443 Y-4.801 Z-10 F300  ...
G0 X77.479 Y-5.695 Z25        (end of op)
```
Bottom Z is world -0.5 (WCS Z-17.5). Verify: ok, no finding. The stock in this run has no XY margin, so nothing flags the uncut sides; with real oversized stock the part stays attached.

**Priority P2, not P3:** it does not gouge, but it is the default whole-model 2D Contour silently ignoring a stated Bottom Z and tabs, with no diagnostic anywhere (generate, verify, post) - the op posts a partial program as complete. Not P1 because it removes less, never more.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** on this part both cases contour the plate outline down to Bottom Z with the tabs written (or each ring that cannot go on is refused/flagged by name with the level it stopped at); pinned by tests on a part whose outline grows below Top Z (chamfered island, open-ended slot floor).

body:
## What happens

A 2D Chamfer with no picked edges, on a model whose edge already carries the modelled chamfer, puts the cone tip on the **top** edge of the chamfer (the top face's outline) and drops it by the width. The tip runs 1 mm inside the island wall. The posted G-code cuts a V into the part, and `verify` says `ok: true`, gouge 0. In the QA run `render_stock` painted the chamfer band as uncut rest, so the sim is not judging the cone that is posted (the edge-break credit appears to accept it as the intended break).

## Expected

Either the chamfer's lower edge (the wall at y = -15, z = 14) is the edge the cone rides, giving tip (y -15, z 14) and the modelled 1 x 1 chamfer, or the op refuses / says the edge is already chamfered. In any case verify must convict a cone that cuts below the model.

## Repro (MCP, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

**Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot.

1. `add_tool {catalog: "CM-1000-90"}` (90 deg taper, D10)
2. `add_operation {kind: "2D Chamfer", tool: "CM-1000-90", source: "flange", params: {width: 1}}` - no picks
3. `generate`, `verify`, `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`

## Evidence (upstream main abe24ff09, same as v0.23.0)

```
G0 X75 Y15.999 Z25
G1 X75 Y15.999 Z-3 F300
G1 X25.05 Y15.999 Z-3 F1200
```
WCS Y15.999 / Z-3 is world y = -14.001, z = 14. The island wall is at y = -15; the chamfer surface runs from (y -15, z 14) to (y -14, z 15). A 90 deg cone with its tip at (-14, 14) reaches 0.71 mm normal into the chamfer face (it cuts a ~2 x 2 chamfer with a V below the modelled one). With `width: 0.5` the XY stays at Y15.999 and only Z changes (Z-2.5), so the width never moves the ride off the top edge.

`verify` on the same program: `ok: true`, findings `[]`, gate ok.

Workaround seen by the QA run: pick the chamfer's lower edge chain (z = 14) with `set_operation_geometry`; that posts `Y15 Z-3`, which is correct, and the sim is clean. `set_operation_area {offset: 1}` is refused ("a 2D Chamfer's cone lies on the picked wall - its ride cannot be offset or clipped").

Priority P1: posted G-code that cuts into the part and passes verify (Prime Directive). Related: #303, #529, #1891 (edge-break records and their credit).

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** the no-pick 2D Chamfer on a model with a modelled chamfer either rides the chamfer's lower edge (tip at the wall) or refuses by name; and a chamfer cone that cuts below the model is a blocking verify finding, not edge-break credit. Pinned by a test on this geometry (tip XY/Z asserted, verify verdict asserted).

body:
Asked for by Mike (collaborator) on 2026-11-18, after a Windows 11 user's "it kept crashing" report: "We should add some/most of that in a FAQ or Windows Troubleshooting on CamCraft docs for Windows users."

A new page in the user guide (site/content/guide/, linked from the install page and the FAQ), plain language:

1. **The app does not start or closes at once:** start it with another graphics backend - a shortcut with `--gpu-backend dx12`, `vulkan` or `gl` added to Target. What each means, in one line each.
2. **The whole PC freezes, the screen shows "snow"** (seen on a desktop Ryzen 5 with onboard Radeon): this is a graphics driver or hardware hang that CamCraft's 3D view triggers, not a CamCraft crash. Checks, in order: the latest AMD/Intel/NVIDIA driver from the vendor's site; onboard graphics use main RAM, so try the BIOS RAM profile (XMP/EXPO) off and set "UMA Frame Buffer Size" to 2-4 GB; BIOS update; temperatures.
3. **Testing the PC itself:** free tools by name and what each tests - MemTest86 (RAM, from USB), OCCT (CPU/RAM/graphics with temperatures), HWiNFO64 (temperatures). Note: save work first.
4. **What to send us:** `dxdiag` -> "Save All Information" (note it contains the PC name), the CamCraft log file and where it is (once #2421 lands), the version, and the step where it failed. Where to send it (GitHub issue or Discord).
5. **Windows on ARM / virtual machines:** the x64 build runs under emulation; it worked on a Parallels ARM VM using the software renderer, slower.

Done means: the page exists in the guide, is linked from the install page, and builds with `zola build`. No claims we have not tested; tools are named, not endorsed.

body:
A Windows 11 user reported that v0.23.0 "kept crashing" and uninstalled it. We had nothing to go on: no log, no GPU, no step.

A check on a second Windows 11 machine (Intel Arc 140T + NVIDIA RTX 5050 laptop, v0.23.0 zip) found the app runs there with the default, dx12 and vulkan backends, so the crash is likely tied to the user's GPU/driver. It also found:

4. If startup fails on one backend, the error says which `--gpu-backend` values to try.

Done means: launching on Windows without a terminal leaves a log file that names the adapter and backend, and a forced startup failure (e.g. `--gpu-backend` set to a backend the machine lacks) leaves its error in that log. Pinned by a test of the log setup where it can be tested headlessly.

- the rough's rings close without a second lap (or each ring unwinds: lift, turn A back, go on), so a level stays inside 720 degrees; or

## What happens

Found in the full review of PR #517 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/517#pullrequestreview-5910390160), note "Old projects".

The refusal tells the user what to do: regenerate the threading operation. Alternative: the stamp carries a generator version, so that such an operation reads Stale.

- A Tormach G76 refusal for a record with `finish_allowance` 0 (a record cached before PR #517) tells the user to regenerate the operation.
- A test posts such a record and asserts the text of the refusal.
- The Fanuc post's behaviour for the same record (it writes `R0`, the output of main before PR #517) does not change in this issue.

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

body:
## What happens
When CamCraft is started from a terminal, the terminal tells you almost nothing
about what the app is doing. There is no logging framework in the workspace at
all: no `log` or `tracing` dependency in any Cargo.toml, no subscriber
init in the binaries - just ~185 ad-hoc `println!`/`eprintln!` calls scattered
across crates (cli.rs, gpu_init.rs, shell.rs, the post bin). If a subsystem
decides, refuses, retries, or fails to write a file, no line reaches the
console and the failure is only discovered later by forensics on the output.

## Why now (session of 2026-11-07)
Two incidents this week were diagnosed only by reading source afterwards,
because the console was silent during them:
- **A file did not get saved when post processing** - the post appeared to
  succeed; nothing in the terminal said which path it wrote (or that it wrote
  nothing at all).
- **A limit was hit while generating operations** - the generator aborted on a
  budget/limit; the terminal showed no trace of which cap fired or what the
  result was downgraded to.

Prime Directive says "log diagnostics, never silence" - today we cannot.

## Expected
The launching terminal streams debug-level logs of app activity, filterable:
- project save / post write: source path, destination, bytes, or the reason
  nothing was written;
- operation generation: start, end, duration, which limits/budgets stopped a
  generator and what fallback took over;
- verify/sim refusals: the rule that fired and the numbers behind it;
- commands executing (name + affected entities) at debug level.

## Suggested shape
`tracing` + `tracing_subscriber` fmt layer writing to stderr at startup of the
UI binary, default level `info`, overridable by `RUST_LOG` (or a camcraft
config/env of our own). Instrument the command dispatch seam, generators, and
post entry points - the crates are already split (M4.1), so each takes its own
span targets (`camcraft_app::post`, `camcraft_motion::adaptive`, ...). Keep
hot generation loops behind level gates - logging must not slow generation.

## Done means
- Launching the app and running a post writes terminal lines naming the file
  path and result; a failed/skipped write says why.
- Hitting a generation budget (e.g. an Adaptive limit) prints which limit and
  what happened next.
- Levels are controlled by env var, default output stays quiet at `info`, and
  the batch gate shows no measurable generation slowdown.

Found while debugging the post-save incident (user request, 2026-11-07).
